$schema: See scripts/audit/gate.mjs. Every entry needs ghsa, package, severity, reason, link, expires.
$comment: Accepted supply-chain risk, with a date on it.
An entry here means: this advisory is high or critical, it is in a dependency this
product ships, and there is no fix we can take today. It does NOT mean the finding is
harmless. Read `reason` for the reachability argument that was actually checked
against this codebase, and docs/DECISION_LOG.md 'Supply chain' for the long form.
`expires` is enforced. On the day after it passes, CI goes red and stays red until
somebody re-triages and either fixes the finding or re-dates the entry with a fresh
reason. There is no way to let one of these rot quietly, which is the specific failure
Not listed here, and deliberately: `next` itself. Its own advisories cleared when the
repo moved to 16.2.12. What is left below reaches the tree THROUGH next, as bundled
transitive dependencies with no independently upgradable version.

entries.reason: XSS via an unescaped </style> in PostCSS stringify output. postcss reaches this tree only through next and @tailwindcss/postcss, where it runs at build time over CSS this repository authors. The advisory needs attacker-controlled CSS; no user input reaches the Tailwind pipeline. No upgradable version exists that is not a next downgrade.

Arbitrary file read via an attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL in a CSS comment. Same build-time-only reachability as the entry above: the CSS PostCSS parses is app/globals.css plus Tailwind output, all of it in this repository. No stable fix available that is not a next downgrade.

Path traversal in previous-source-map auto-loading, disclosing arbitrary .map files. Requires attacker-controlled CSS or map references at build time; the build runs on CI over repository-controlled sources only. Same absent upstream fix as the other two postcss entries.

Inherited libvips CVEs (CVE-2026-33327/33328/35590/35591). sharp is an optional dependency of next used only by the image optimizer. next/image is not used anywhere in this app (components/TaskCard.tsx documents the deliberate avoidance) and next.config.ts configures no remote image hosts, so the decoder is reachable only through the default optimizer endpoint with no allowed remote sources. No stable next release ships a patched sharp yet.
